## Item 43 — Reimbursable pass-through: an "exclude from Analysis" category flag

- **Status:** PLANNED, not started — **grilled to build-ready 2026-07-22** (promoted from IDEA the same day; the original "Receivables & Payables module" framing was scoped *down* by the grill — see below). **Build on Opus, medium effort** — multi-feature and cross-ADR (redacting view + sync + three aggregation surfaces + the `is_settlement` precedent), so Opus per CLAUDE.md, though the grill has retired most of the design risk (it's now closer to a careful sweep than a novel design). **Needs a short new ADR** defining the "exclude from analysis" category property + its exclusion boundary before/with the build.
- **Request:** Alvin asked whether the app covers "expenses reimbursable by my employer." Today it doesn't cleanly: you front a work expense, it shows as **spending** in Analysis; the employer pays you back, it shows as **income** — but it's a pass-through, neither is truly yours, so both distort your charts.
- **Grill outcome (the scope-down):** the "full Receivables & Payables module" (counterparty entity, pending/settled status, running totals like Partner Debt) was **rejected** — same call as personal-loans (no new entity; see Product Decisions memory). The grill established the *real* itch is **(a) un-pollute Analysis**, not (b) a pending tracker or (c) a full external IOU ledger. Chosen model is **pass-through / static**: a reimbursable is *never* counted in Analysis regardless of whether it's been paid back yet — so **no status, no counterparty, no new entity**. This is the exact semantic of the existing `is_settlement` flag ("hidden from Analysis, still real money"), lifted to the category level.
- **Mechanism:** one new boolean `exclude_from_analysis` on **`categories`**, available on **both** expense and income category types (both legs must be excludable — an expense-only flag would let the payback re-pollute the income/net side via `DailyNetCalculator`). Category-editor toggle, labeled neutrally **"Exclude from spending reports"** (not "Reimbursable" — reads wrong on an income category), helper text naming reimbursements as the headline example: *"For pass-through money like work expenses your employer pays back — kept in your balance, hidden from charts and budgets."* **Pre-seed a "Reimbursable" (expense) + "Reimbursement" (income) category pair** in the onboarding Templates step with the flag set, so the feature is discoverable without spelunking the editor.
- **Exclusion boundary (the spec — mirrors `is_settlement`):**
  - **Records ledger — shows ✅** (it's a real transaction you made).
  - **Account balance — counts ✅** (money genuinely moved; keeps balance honest while you await repayment).
  - **Analysis (donut / expense-flow / calendar-net) — excluded ❌.**
  - **Budgets (`BudgetProgressCalculator`) — excluded ❌** (a work expense shouldn't eat your personal budget).
  - **Couple Combined view (`CombinedLedgerCalculator`) — excluded ❌** (not real household shared spending).
- **Gating:** **free, unconditional** — not in the paywall feature map. It's basic bookkeeping accuracy (same class as creating/assigning a category); gating it would leave a free user's Analysis knowingly wrong, against the "recording your own money is never gated" principle (ADR-0044).
- **Build shape (calculators stay pure):** at the three feature boundaries that already observe categories (Analysis, Budgets, Combined), derive `excludedCategoryIds = categories.filter { it.excludeFromAnalysis }.map { it.id }` and drop matching transactions *before* handing off to the calculator — factored into one small, tier-1-testable helper so all three surfaces stay consistent. Also **hide excluded categories from the budget-category picker.** Note: `BudgetProgressCalculator.spent()` currently filters only type/category/cycle (it doesn't even honor `is_settlement`), so the budget exclusion is genuinely new filtering regardless of approach.
- **Combined handling (decided — exclude, "Option A", grilled 2026-07-22):** Combined shows *both partners' non-private* transactions (`ObserveCombinedTransactionsUseCase`), so a reimbursable expense reaches it unless stopped. We exclude it (not "just let it show") — the feature's whole point is that reimbursables aren't real spending, and the couple view is exactly where an inflated shared-spend number would mislead. Mechanism: `CombinedLedgerCalculator.spendFor()` (which today only takes `categoryNames`) also takes an `excludedCategoryIds: Set<String>` and `continue`s on match; the set is derived from the combined category map the ViewModel *already* holds to label partner rows, so it naturally covers **both** partners' excluded categories — which is exactly why the redacting-view fix below is load-bearing.
- **Cross-ADR catch (do not miss):** the **partner-category redacting view (ADR-0004/0005) must expose the new `exclude_from_analysis` column** (a one-line add alongside `name`/`type`/`icon`/`color` in the `partner_categories` view), or Combined cannot see the *partner's* flag and can't exclude their reimbursables. The flag otherwise syncs as an ordinary `categories` column (ADR-0009 push/pull order unchanged).
- **Sweep surface:** category editor screen + `CategoryEntity`/`CategoryDto`/`CategoryMapper` (+ partner variants); `supabase/schema.sql` (new column + partner redacting view); the three calculator feed points (`AnalysisCalculator`/`ExpenseFlowCalculator`/`DailyNetCalculator`, `CombinedLedgerCalculator`, `BudgetProgressCalculator`); onboarding Templates seed. **Room v27 → v28.**
- **Verify:** tier-1 tests for the new filter helper (transactions in excluded categories dropped; non-excluded pass through; empty/none sets) and a mapper round-trip for the new column; confirm balance derivation is unaffected (reimbursable rows still counted). On-device: a reimbursable expense + its matching reimbursement income both vanish from donut/flow/calendar/budgets/Combined while still appearing in Records and moving account balance; the seeded category pair renders in onboarding Templates.

## Item 44 — Bump targetSdk 35 → 36 (Android 16) for Google Play's Aug 2026 target-API requirement

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `18a9ed7`** (2026-07-22, booked Sonnet / ran on Opus this session, low–medium effort). Code committed green; **on-device edge-to-edge walk on a real API 36 device is still Alvin's gate before the prod release.** No schema/Room change (stays **v27**). The bump is one line; the effort is the inset verification it triggers, not the code.
- **Build outcome:** [app/build.gradle.kts:27](../../app/build.gradle.kts#L27) `targetSdk = 35` → `36`, single line. `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` both green (no new tests — pure config change, no domain/sync/money logic touched). **Inset code-walk done (low regression risk found):** the app already opts into edge-to-edge explicitly — `enableEdgeToEdge()` in both [MainActivity.kt:167](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/MainActivity.kt#L167) and [QuickAddActivity.kt:54](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/widget/presentation/QuickAddActivity.kt#L54), the global `Scaffold` passes `contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets(0,0,0,0)` and each screen manages its own insets (`statusBarsPadding()` on every title-bearing top-level screen; the custom `PlayfulBottomBar` consumes `WindowInsets.navigationBars` at [IponApp.kt:568](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/IponApp.kt#L568) via the `44e7fd5` follow-up), and the chrome-less Budgets/Accounts/Categories/Combined bodies inherit their host's status-bar padding — so the app never relied on the opt-out API 36 removes, making the bump behaviorally inert for insets. On-device confirmation on a real API 36 device stays the ship gate.
- **Request:** hours after the v1.6.7 closed-testing release, Google Play emailed Alvin the "Your app is affected by Google Play's target API level requirements" warning — Love, Ipon targets an old Android version and must meet the target-API minimum before **Aug 31, 2026**. That deadline's minimum is **API level 36 (Android 16)**; the app currently sets `targetSdk = 35` ([app/build.gradle.kts:27](../../app/build.gradle.kts#L27)). Not blocking yet (updates targeting 35 are still accepted until the deadline, ~5½ weeks out), but the next release should clear it. Deliberately **not** slipped into the v1.6.8 widget-fix AAB — behavior changes need their own tested item.
- **Change:**
  - [app/build.gradle.kts:27](../../app/build.gradle.kts#L27) — `targetSdk = 35` → `36`. `compileSdk` is already **37**, so no SDK-platform/toolchain work is needed (compileSdk ≥ targetSdk holds).
  - **Behavior-change surface to check (this is the real work):** targeting API 36 opts the app into Android 16 behavior changes — chiefly **mandatory edge-to-edge** (the framework stops honoring opt-out of drawing behind the status/nav bars), plus stricter large-screen/orientation handling and background-work rules. Because the Playful Pop reskin recently reworked window insets (v1.6.7 Item 8 + the nav-bar-inset follow-up `44e7fd5`), walk the app for content drawing under or clipped by the system bars and fix any inset regressions at the affected composables/`Scaffold`s. No new ADR — this is a platform-compliance bump, not an architecture decision.
  - **Does not change:** minSdk (stays 26), any feature logic, the paywall/entitlement seam, or sync.
- **Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green (pure config change — existing tests just need to still pass; no new tier-1 test — no domain/sync/money logic touched). **On-device is the gate:** install on a real device / emulator running **Android 16 (API 36)** if available (else the highest available) and walk every top-level surface — Records, Analysis, Budgets, Accounts, Categories, Notes, Couple/Combined, Settings, Add/Edit-txn full-screen route, and the home-screen widgets' host — confirming nothing draws under the status/nav bars, no clipped headers/FABs, and the keyboard/IME insets still behave. Fix any edge-to-edge regressions before it ships. Pure Composable/inset verification → verified by running, not unit-tested.

## Item 45 — Fix: partner-debt settlement legs leak into the *overall* budget

- **Status:** PLANNED, not started. **Sonnet, low effort** — a one-line filter fix + a tier-1 test; mechanical, no design risk. **Found while grilling [Item 43](#item-43--reimbursable-pass-through-an-exclude-from-analysis-category-flag)** (2026-07-22) — booked separately because it's a pre-existing bug unrelated to reimbursements, not part of that feature.
- **Bug:** [BudgetProgressCalculator.spent()](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/domain/usecase/BudgetProgressCalculator.kt) filters only by `type == EXPENSE`, category, and cycle — it honors **no** exclusion flag. A partner-debt **settlement** leg (ADR-0019 #14 / ADR-0042) is a real `EXPENSE` carrying `categoryId = null` and `is_settlement = true`. For an **overall** budget (`categoryId == null`), the calculator's `budget.categoryId == null || it.categoryId == budget.categoryId` branch counts *all* expenses, so a debt repayment counts against the overall budget — even though every Analysis calculator (`AnalysisCalculator`/`ExpenseFlowCalculator`/`DailyNetCalculator`/`CombinedLedgerCalculator`) already excludes `is_settlement` as "not spending." Per-category budgets are unaffected (a null-category leg matches no specific category).
- **Fix:** add `.filter { !it.isSettlement }` to `BudgetProgressCalculator.spent()`, mirroring the exclusion the Analysis calculators already apply. No schema/Room/sync change (stays **v27**).
- **Verify:** tier-1 test — an overall budget's `spent` excludes a settlement-flagged expense while still counting a normal one; a per-category budget's result is unchanged.
- **Sequencing vs Item 43:** both touch the same `spent()` method — 43 adds a reimbursable-category exclusion there too. If 45 lands first it's the minimal fix; if built together the two exclusions fold into one filter. Land 45 first (smaller, independent) unless building 43 makes it convenient to do both at once.
